problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+4{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+4{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)+4\cdot (-1\cdot (-2))+4\cdot (1\cdot k) \\  & =-4+8+4k \\  & =4+4k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ 4+4k & =0 \\ 4k & =-4 \\ k & =-1\end{aligned}
$$
